The message you're seeing is a billing notice from the Freebuff client, not a code issue: the GPT-6 Luna hour you bought is currently attached to a different tab, and a second hour can't start while that one is active. Nothing is broken, and nothing has been charged twice.

To continue here, click **“Use it here”** in this tab — that moves the *remaining* time from the other tab to this one at no extra cost. The alternative is to switch back to the other tab and keep working there. Note that moving it will end the session in the other tab, so don't do it mid-run there.

On the actual task from before the failed turn — enhancing page loading speed — nothing was done yet, so there are no edits to reconcile or undo in the project. Once the hour is moved into this tab, I'll start by measuring where the load time actually goes (server components vs. client bundles, image sizes, font loading) and then apply the highest-impact fixes rather than guessing.

{"kind":"reasoning","id":"p5-9450f92a","text":"Big findings so far:

1. Home page: `"use client"` + `useEffect` fetch for posts => the entire homepage ships as a client component, with a client-side data fetch after hydration. That's a big LCP issue: posts list not in initial HTML, skeleton flash, client bundle huge (whole page markup + i18n messages). This is the biggest win: make the home page a server component that fetches posts on the server. With cacheComponents enabled, we can use `use cache` or just fetch from the data layer directly.

2. `d-buckky-moral.png` is 2.2MB for a 190px-wide image — next/image will optimize it, but as a public asset next/image optimizes on demand (works). But width=1200 height=1200 with sizes 190px — the browser gets an optimized version. Still the source is 2.2MB. Better: resize the asset. Actually next/image in dev/prod optimizes. But the optimizer must read 2.2MB and compress it each first request; also if `unoptimized` anywhere. Let's check whether they use `images: { unoptimized: true }` — no config for images, so optimizer is on. Fine, but reducing the source is still a win, plus avoids layout shift concerns. Priority: not marked priority, so it's lazy — fine.

3. Home page hero image `daily-essential-white.png` is 4000x1009 declared with `priority` — served at w=160/192 via next/image optimizer. OK.

5. Fonts: Geist + Geist_Mono loaded in root layout, two font families. Geist_Mono may be unused → remove one font to cut a network request and CSS.

6. `partialPrefetching: true` and `cacheComponents: true` already set.

title: cacheLife
description: Learn how to use the cacheLife function to set the cache expiration time for a cached function or component.
related:
  title: Related
  description: View related API references.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
    - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag
---

The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component.

## Usage

### Basic setup

To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:

```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
}

export default nextConfig
```

```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
const nextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
}

module.exports = nextConfig
```

`cacheLife` can only be used within a cache directive scope.

Add a cache directive (for example, `use cache`) at the file level or at the top of an async function or component.

`cacheLife` cannot be used at module scope. Calling it at the top level of a file will throw an error.

> **Good to know**:
>
> - We recommend setting a `cacheLife` in every `use cache` scope so its behavior is clear at the call site. Omitting it leaves the lifetime implicit (the `default` profile applies), which makes it harder to reason about, for example in [nested cached scopes](#nested-caching-behavior).
> - Call `cacheLife` in the same function or component where caching is defined. Avoid abstracting it into shared utilities so the cache behavior remains explicit and easy to reason about.
> - If you call `cacheLife`, ensure only one call executes per function invocation. You can call it in different control flow branches, but only one should run per request. See the [conditional cache lifetimes](#conditional-cache-lifetimes) example.

### Using preset profiles

Next.js provides preset cache profiles that cover common caching needs. Each profile balances three factors:

- How long users see cached content without checking for updates (client-side)
- How often fresh content is generated on the server
- When old content expires completely

Choose a profile based on how frequently your content changes:

- **`seconds`** - Real-time data (stock prices, live scores)
- **`minutes`** - Frequently updated (social feeds, news)
- **`hours`** - Multiple daily updates (product inventory, weather)
- **`days`** - Daily updates (blog posts, articles)
- **`weeks`** - Weekly updates (podcasts, newsletters)
- **`max`** - Rarely changes (legal pages, archived content)

Import `cacheLife` and pass a profile name:

```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" highlight={1,5}
'use cache'
import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'

export default async function BlogPage() {
  cacheLife('days') // Blog content updated daily

  const posts = await getBlogPosts()
  return <div>{/* render posts */}</div>
}

The `opengraph-image` and `twitter-image` file conventions allow you to set Open Graph and Twitter images for a route segment.

There are two ways to set Open Graph and Twitter images:

- [Using image files (.jpg, .png, .gif)](#image-files-jpg-png-gif)
- [Using code to generate images (.js, .ts, .tsx)](#generate-images-using-code-js-ts-tsx)

In addition to using [literal image files](#image-files-jpg-png-gif), you can programmatically **generate** images using code.

{"kind":"tool","id":"kLgbbFMZg7E","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/lib/seo.ts","instructions":"Add shared SEO helpers: canonical URLs, hreflang alternates, page metadata and article structured data.","content":"import type { Metadata } from "next";
import { messages, type Locale } from "@/lib/i18n";
import type { Post } from "@/lib/parse";

/** Single source of truth for absolute URLs (sitemap, robots, canonicals, OG tags). */
export const SITE_URL = (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL || "https://dailyessential.ch").replace(/\/+$/, "");
export const SITE_NAME = "Daily Essential";
export const DEFAULT_OG_IMAGE = "/d-buckky-moral.png";
export const OG_IMAGE_SIZE = { width: 2000, height: 2000 };

const OG_LOCALES: Record<Locale, string> = { en: "en_CH", fr: "fr_CH", ar: "ar_AR" };

/** Every localised route hides behind its locale prefix; these are the canonical paths. */
export function localePath(locale: Locale, path = "") {
  return `/${locale}${path}`;
}

/** Absolute URL for a locale route, used in canonicals and structured data. */
export function absoluteUrl(locale: Locale, path = "") {
  return `${SITE_URL}${localePath(locale, path)}`;
}

/**
 * hreflang map for a page path ("" for the home page). Every locale exists for the
 * shared pages, so a visitor landing on a French URL can be pointed at its siblings.
 */
export function languageAlternates(path = "") {
  return {
    en: localePath("en", path),
    fr: localePath("fr", path),
    ar: localePath("ar", path),
    "x-default": localePath("en", path),
  };
}

type PageMetadataInput = {
  locale: Locale;
  path?: string;
  title: string;
  description: string;
};

export function pageMetadata({ locale, path = "", title, description }: PageMetadataInput): Metadata {
  const url = localePath(locale, path);
  const image = { url: DEFAULT_OG_IMAGE, ...OG_IMAGE_SIZE, alt: SITE_NAME };

  return {
    title,
    description,
    alternates: { canonical: url, languages: languageAlternates(path) },
    openGraph: {
      type: "website",
      siteName: SITE_NAME,
      locale: OG_LOCALES[locale],
      url,
      title,
      description,
      images: [image],
    },
    twitter: { card: "summary_large_image", title, description, images: [DEFAULT_OG_IMAGE] },
  };
}

/** Home-page metadata: the site name carries the title, the tagline carries the description. */
export function homeMetadata(locale: Locale): Metadata {
  const copy = messages[locale];
  return pageMetadata({
    locale,
    path: "",
    title: `${SITE_NAME} | ${copy.home.latestPosts}`,
    description: `${copy.home.authorLead} ${copy.home.exploreHeading}`,
  });
}

/** Article structured data, so search results can show headline, date and author. */
export function articleJsonLd(post: Post, locale: Locale, description: string) {
  return {
    "@context": "https://schema.org",
    "@type": "Article",
    headline: post.title,
    description,
    inLanguage: locale,
    ...(post.publishedAt ? { datePublished: post.publishedAt, dateModified: post.publishedAt } : {}),
    ...(post.coverImage ? { image: [post.coverImage] } : {}),
    articleSection: post.category,
    author: { "@type": "Person", name: messages[locale].author.name },
    publisher: { "@type": "Organization", name: SITE_NAME, url: SITE_URL },
    isPartOf: { "@type": "WebSite", name: SITE_NAME, url: SITE_URL },
    mainEntityOfPage: { "@type": "WebPage", "@id": absoluteUrl(locale, `/posts/${post.slug}`) },
  };
}

/** JSON-LD is embedded in a <script> tag, so "</script>" must not survive stringification. */
export function jsonLd(value: unknown) {
  return JSON.stringify(value).replace(/</g, "\\u003c");
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"kLil2c3ljBw","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/app/sitemap.ts","instructions":"Rewrite sitemap with hreflang alternates, env-based URL and deduplicated post entries.","content":"import type { MetadataRoute } from "next";
import { locales } from "@/lib/i18n";
import { getPosts } from "@/lib/parse";
import { SITE_URL, localePath, languageAlternates } from "@/lib/seo";

const pages = [
  { path: "", priority: 1 },
  { path: "/about", priority: 0.8 },
  { path: "/author", priority: 0.9 },
  { path: "/contact", priority: 0.8 },
  { path: "/ebooks", priority: 0.9 },
  { path: "/faq", priority: 0.6 },
  { path: "/marketplace", priority: 0.5 },
  { path: "/privacy", priority: 0.3 },
  { path: "/shop", priority: 0.5 },
  { path: "/terms", priority: 0.3 },
];

/** One `<url>` per locale route, each advertising its siblings as hreflang alternates. */
const staticRoutes: MetadataRoute.Sitemap = pages.flatMap((page) =>
  locales.map((locale) => ({
    url: `${SITE_URL}${localePath(locale, page.path)}`,
    changeFrequency: "weekly" as const,
    priority: page.priority,
    alternates: { languages: languageAlternates(page.path) },
  })),
);

export default async function sitemap(): Promise<MetadataRoute.Sitemap> {
  const fallback = staticRoutes;
  try {
    const posts = await getPosts();
    const postRoutes: MetadataRoute.Sitemap = posts.map((post) => {
      const locale = post.locale === "fr" || post.locale === "ar" ? post.locale : "en";
      return {
        url: `${SITE_URL}/${locale}/posts/${post.slug}`,
        lastModified: post.publishedAt ? new Date(post.publishedAt) : undefined,
        changeFrequency: "monthly" as const,
        priority: 0.7,
      };
    });
    // De-duplicate: a post reachable through two locales would otherwise repeat.
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    return [...fallback, ...postRoutes].filter((entry) => {
      if (seen.has(entry.url)) return false;
      seen.add(entry.url);
      return true;
    });
  } catch {
    return fallback;
  }
}

+/** Home-page metadata: the site name carries the title, the tagline carries the description. */
+export function homeMetadata(locale: Locale): Metadata {
+  const copy = messages[locale];
+  return pageMetadata({
+    locale,
+    path: "",
+    title: `${SITE_NAME} | ${copy.home.latestPosts}`,
+    description: `${copy.home.authorLead} ${copy.home.exploreHeading}`,
+  });

+/** Article structured data, so search results can show headline, date and author. */
+export function articleJsonLd(post: Post, locale: Locale, description: string) {
+  return {
+    "@context": "https://schema.org",
+    "@type": "Article",
+    headline: post.title,
+    description,
+    inLanguage: locale,
+    ...(post.publishedAt ? { datePublished: post.publishedAt, dateModified: post.publishedAt } : {}),
+    ...(post.coverImage ? { image: [post.coverImage] } : {}),
+    articleSection: post.category,
+    author: { "@type": "Person", name: messages[locale].author.name },
+    publisher: { "@type": "Organization", name: SITE_NAME, url: SITE_URL },
+    isPartOf: { "@type": "WebSite", name: SITE_NAME, url: SITE_URL },
+    mainEntityOfPage: { "@type": "WebPage", "@id": absoluteUrl(locale, `/posts/${post.slug}`) },
+  };
+}

+/** JSON-LD is embedded in a <script> tag, so "</script>" must not survive stringification. */
